title.narrative: Strengthening Evidence-Based Policymaking for Education Sector Reforms

description.narrative: Current approaches to decision-making in Belarus’s education sector rely on methods of evidence utilization and analysis that are not in line with international best practices. Sharp and continued student population decline and urbanization in a severely constrained fiscal environment requires the introduction of modern mechanisms of resource allocation—such as Per Student Financing (PSF)—that are adaptable to the actual demand for education services in the country. Howevercomma the Ministries of Education and Finance lack adequate analytical and technical capacity for fully implementing such reforms. Furthermorecomma a country that aspires to efficiently provide high-quality education to its population needs well-developed systems of quality assessment that accurately measure student learning levels. Yet little hard evidence exists about the quality of education in Belarus; the country remains the last holdout in Europe to have never participated in international assessments of student learning. The World Bank’s recent PER “Belarus Public Expenditure Review: Enhancing Public Services in Times of Austerity” (2013) concluded that the country needs to continue to right-size the school networkcomma gradually move to per-student based financingcomma and strengthen accountability for results. The Government of Belarus (GoB) has committed to introducing the necessary education sector reforms and transforming it into a moderncomma cost-effective and high-quality sector. The GoB has requested the Bank’s support in preparing these reforms. The Development Objective of this grant is to lay the groundwork for future Education Sector Reforms with the help of modern approaches to evidence-based policymaking through improved (i) data collection and analysis; (ii) financing; and (iii) quality assessment.
